entries.title: Unweighted refresh energy has a first-order spectral floor
entries.statement: For a square-integrable function f of finitely many independent coordinates, let f_S be its orthogonal coordinate-average product projections. Refresh each coordinate independently at rate one, and set C_f(t)=Cov(f(W),f(W^t)), E_f(t)=-C_f'(t), and H_f(t)=exp(t)E_f(t). Then L=sum_{|S|=1}||f_S||_2^2 is the limit of H_f(t), R_f(t)=H_f(t)-L=sum_{|S|>=2}|S|exp(-(|S|-1)t)||f_S||_2^2 is nonnegative, and Var(f)=L+integral_0^infinity exp(-t)R_f(t)dt. If L>0, no bound H_f(t)<=A F(Bt) for all t>=0 can hold with finite positive A,B and a nonnegative integrable F. The weighted energy E_f itself tends to zero; the floor concerns the unweighted convention only.
entries.proof_text: The independent refresh operator multiplies each f_S by exp(-|S|t), and orthogonality gives C_f(t)=sum_{S nonempty}exp(-|S|t)||f_S||^2. Differentiate the finite sum, multiply by exp(t), and separate |S|=1. Integrating the remaining terms gives their squared norms. If the proposed envelope held with L>0, then F(s)>=L/A for all s>=0, contradicting integrability. Independently rederived by w362; its exact square reproduction has L=1/4 and variance 23/64.

entries.title: DRAFT: separate first-order energy in the FPP crossover route
entries.statement: For iid Uniform[1,2] undirected nearest-neighbor Z^2 FPP, T_n=T(0,n e1), let the UNWEIGHTED refresh kernel be H_n(t)=exp(t)(-C_n'(t)), L_n its first-order spectral limit, and R_n=H_n-L_n. A sufficient conditional route to variance comparable to n^(2/3) is: L_n<=C n^(2/3); R_n(t)<=C n F(n^(1/3)t) for every t>=0 with one nonnegative integrable F; and H_n(t)>=c n for 0<=t<=c' n^(-1/3). Constants are independent of n. The separated variance identity gives upper bound C n^(2/3)(1+integral F) and lower bound c c' exp(-c') n^(2/3). ALL THREE quantitative inputs remain unproved. The earlier all-time integrable envelope on the full unweighted H_n ignores a positive first-order floor and is infeasible; do not promote this corrected conditional route into a proof of its inputs or a solution of P0104.
assumptions: the specified bounded planar FPP model
all three unproved crossover inputs with uniform constants
entries.domain: probability, first-passage percolation, draft conditional proof route

relations.rationale: The route explicitly uses 'L_n its first-order spectral limit, and R_n=H_n-L_n'; the lemma supplies 'Var(f)=L+integral_0^infinity exp(-t)R_f(t)dt'. This separation repairs the impossible full-unweighted-kernel envelope; the quantitative inputs remain unproved.
